text:
The Penguins are 7-13-2, winless in three and 2-7-1 over their last ten, and the conversation in Pittsburgh has moved from the standings to the sell-off. The Post-Gazette's first-quarter report card gave low marks to Sidney Crosby and Erik Karlsson, RMNB writes that the team is preparing for a potential fire sale with hard decisions on Evgeni Malkin and Kris Letang, and Elliotte Friedman reported that Rickard Rakell blocked a deal to Chicago that involved a first-round pick and Teuvo Teravainen. Ottawa has since been linked to Rakell and Bryan Rust. Even Crosby's future is being debated, with Montreal speculation growing after comments from his agent, Pat Brisson.

Here's the part that stings: the play has been better than the record. Pittsburgh has 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 52% at 5v5, and by our numbers it deserved about six more points than it has. The finishing is 7 goals short of its chances. The recent stretch is less forgiving, though: 43% of the expected goals in this skid, and Arturs Silovs is at .847 and 4.5 goals worse than expected over his last five starts (0-4-1).

Crosby's line with Rakell and Tommy Novak still drives play (59% of shot attempts), and the Malkin, Novak and Egor Chinakhov group wins 56% of expected goals. Our playoff odds are 7%. What we'd watch now is who is still wearing the sweater in March.
